papers.title: Time-and-band limiting for symmetric classical Dunkl orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: The problem of ''time-and-band limiting'' has been previously considered for expansions in orthonormal polynomials that are common eigenfunctions of some second order differential operator. In this paper we consider the situation of orthonormal polynomials that are eigenfunctions of some second order differential-difference operator as introduced by Ch. Dunkl. These polynomials appear already in the work of G. Szeg\H{o} and at the same time play a role in supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Long lived QNM for multiple black holes
papers.abstract: We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.

papers.title: Absence of uniform bounds for the boundary nodal count of Steklov eigenfunctions on Euclidean domains
papers.abstract: We prove that for any $K,N\in\mathbb N$ there exist smooth bounded domains in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq 3$, homeomorphic to a ball, for which the first $N$ positive Steklov eigenvalues are simple and the boundary traces of the corresponding eigenfunctions have at least $K$ nodal domains. This provides a negative answer to the question of whether the number of nodal domains of Dirichlet-to-Neumann eigenfunctions satisfies a Courant-type bound in the Euclidean setting and complements the results of [6].

papers.title: On the self-adjointness of two-dimensional relativistic shell interactions
papers.abstract: We discuss the self-adjointness of the two-dimensional Dirac operator with a transmission condition along a closed Lipschitz curve. The main new ingredients are an explicit use of the Cauchy transform on non-smooth curves and a direct link with the Fredholmness of a singular boundary integral operator. The new self-adjointness condition includes and extends all previous results for this class of problems. The study is particularly precise for the case of curvilinear polygons, as the angles can be taken into account in an explicit way.

papers.title: Universal operators on Banach spaces
papers.abstract: The paper studies universal operators and $n$-tuples of operators on Banach spaces. In the Hilbert-space setting, sufficient criteria for universality, concrete examples, and spectral properties are well established. We investigate extensions of these results to Banach spaces. In particular, we discuss the link between universality and the invariant subspace problem: this leads us to define a stronger notion of universality which is the notion of hereditarily universal operators. We give sufficient conditions for an operator to be hereditarily universal and provide some examples. We also study $n$-tuples of operators by generalizing Vladimir M\"uller's results to the Banach setting. Finally, we obtain a result on the essential spectrum of a universal $n$-tuple of operators on $\ell_p$.

papers.title: Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
papers.abstract: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.

papers.title: Cwikel and Kato-Seiler-Simon estimates for commutators
papers.abstract:
We prove that the commutator $[a(X),b(-\mathrm{i}
abla)]$ belongs to the weak Schatten class $\mathcal{S}^p_{m weak}$ provided $
abla a\in L^p$ and $
abla b\in L^p_{m weak}$ for $\max\{1,2d/(d+2)\}<p<\infty$. This is an analogue of Cwikel's estimate, with a larger range of exponents. We also prove analogues of the Kato-Seiler-Simon and Birman-Solomyak-Simon estimates. Counterexamples show the necessity of the lower thresholds and the failure of the Lipschitz endpoint estimate.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Harper-norm silver-mean conjecture
papers.abstract: The silver-mean conjecture formulated in Gerhold and Shalit 2022 states that the norm $E(\alpha)$ of the Harper operator attains its minimum at the silver mean $\alpha = \sqrt{2}-1$. We show that this conjecture is wrong by constructing an explicit rational point with a smaller Harper-norm value: $E(181/437)<2.591046794<E(\sqrt2-1)$. The separating decimal is an exact rational number. All acceptance checks use exact integer arithmetic with rigorously proved coefficient enclosures. No floating-point eigenvalue estimates or external witness data enter the certificate.

papers.title: Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
papers.abstract: We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.

papers.title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by P\'olya--Szeg\"o
papers.abstract: We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by P\'olya and Szeg\"o: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the partition cells, and with an angular concavity property of this functional on the class of isosceles triangles.

papers.title: Comparing Lower and Upper Spectral Gaps of Nonnegative Symmetric Matrices
papers.abstract: We establish sharp estimates comparing the lower and upper spectral gaps of nonnegative symmetric matrices. Combining these comparisons with a multiplicity argument in the spirit of Li and Liu, we improve and extend earlier spectral gap comparison bounds of Saha and Li and Liu, which provide quantitative refinements of an observation of Breuillard, Green, Guralnick and Tao relating combinatorial expansion to two-sided spectral expansion. Our graph estimates hold for nonbipartite even-walk-regular graphs, which covers the classes of graphs, including vertex-transitive graphs, (twisted) Cayley graphs, and (twisted) Cayley sum graphs, investigated in previous work. Under an additional eigenmap assumption, we also establish quantitative two-sided comparisons between the lower and upper spectral gaps. In particular, these comparisons apply to walk-regular graphs.

papers.title: A Cheng-type Eigenvalue-Comparison Theorem for the Hodge Laplacian
papers.abstract: We consider the class of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with Ricci curvature and injectivity radius bounded below by uniform constants, and an upper bound on the diameter. We establish a uniform upper bound for the eigenvalues of the Hodge Laplacian acting on differential forms on Riemannian manifolds in this class, similar to the classical eigenvalue comparison theorem proved by Cheng for the Laplace-Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions. This extends earlier work of Dodziuk and Lott, which required sectional curvature bounds in addition to bounds on other geometric quantities. As an application, we obtain uniform eigenvalue estimates for the connection Laplacian acting on $1$-forms.
